description: The leads the game proposes: lines of inquiry the player may investigate (docs/case-format.md, Leads). One per line: `text` (plain words, never ahead of the story), `source` (its quotes; a lead is proposed once they are read and its `needs` are held), `scores` (the NOTICE thought it scores for when investigated before Holmes's paragraph; null for a lead that scores nothing).

leads.text: Why was Silver Blaze taken away, when the interest was in keeping him from the race?
source: the singular disappearance of the favourite for the Wessex Cup
preventing Silver Blaze from being there at the fall of the flag

leads.text: The dish of curried mutton at Hunter's supper.
source: his supper, which consisted of a dish of curried mutton

leads.text: Why was Straker's overcoat on a furze-bush?
source: John Straker’s overcoat was flapping from a furze-bush

leads.text: Why did Straker carry a tallow candle as well as his vestas?
source: There was a box of vestas, two inches of tallow candle

leads.text: Why did Straker have a cataract knife?
source: It is what we call a cataract knife

leads.text: Why did Straker carry a bill made out to William Derbyshire?
source: made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire

leads.text: Who ran up thirty-seven pounds fifteen at a Bond Street milliner's?
source: a milliner’s account for thirty-seven pounds fifteen

leads.text: Why have the odds on Silver Blaze shortened?
source: the price has become shorter and shorter
